adjudication_records.issue_text: P1, confidence 75 — [admin/groups_controller.rb:90](/Users/dsifry/Developer/harnesseval/.cache/mrv_repos/9a4f0d24ab144b59/app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90) — `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes an Integer where the ActiveRecord association expects a `User`, causing member removal to fail with a type mismatch/500.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb line 90, the code is `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id = params.require(:user_id).to_i`. The `delete` method on an ActiveRecord association (has_many :users) expects either a record object or an array of record objects, not an integer ID. According to Rails documentation, `collection.delete(object, ...)` removes objects from the collection. Passing an integer ID instead of a User object would not work as expected - it would either fail silently or raise an error depending on Rails version. The correct approach would be `group.users.delete(User.find(user_id))` or using `group.users.where(id: user_id).delete_all`. This is a real bug that would cause member removal to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/scope-and-alignment][lens/intent-preservation] P1, confidence 100 — [group-members.js.es6:8](/Users/dsifry/Developer/harnesseval/.cache/mrv_repos/9a4f0d24ab144b59/app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8) — The public members page fetches only one 50-member page and has no pagination controls, silently hiding subsequent members.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for group-members.js.es6, the setupController calls model.findMembers() which fetches members with pagination (limit/offset). However, examining the template group/members.hbs, it only iterates over 'members' without any pagination controls visible in the template. The admin group template has pagination controls (previous/next buttons with currentPage/totalPages), but the public group members template at discourse/templates/group/members.hbs shows no such pagination UI - it just displays {{#each m in members}}. The findMembers() method in group.js sets limit:50 and offset:0 by default, so only the first 50 members would be shown with no way for users to see more. This is a real functional limitation introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/intent-preservation] P1, confidence 100 — [admin/groups_controller.rb:34](/Users/dsifry/Developer/harnesseval/.cache/mrv_repos/9a4f0d24ab144b59/app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34) — Existing PATCH and nested PUT contracts were silently removed; legacy membership changes are ignored, PATCH can reset `visible` to false, and the endpoint still reports success.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the old code had separate `update_patch` and `update_put` methods that handled PATCH vs PUT requests differently. The `update_patch` method handled incremental membership changes via `params[:changes][:add]` and `params[:changes][:delete]`. The new `update` method completely removes this PATCH handling - it only handles the PUT-style update with `alias_level`, `visible`, and `name` parameters. The finding is correct that the PATCH contract for membership changes was removed. However, the diff also shows that membership management was moved to dedicated endpoints: `add_members` and `remove_member` actions with routes `PUT /members` and `DELETE /members`. So while the old PATCH behavior is removed, it's replaced with new dedicated endpoints. The finding about 'PATCH can reset visible to false' is misleading - the new code handles visible the same way as before. The claim about 'endpoint still reports success' when ignoring membership changes is partially valid - if someone sends the old PATCH format, it would be ignored but return success. This is a real backward compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2, confidence 100 — [groups_controller.rb:22](/Users/dsifry/Developer/harnesseval/.cache/mrv_repos/9a4f0d24ab144b59/app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22) — Unbounded and negative `limit`/`offset` parameters can bypass pagination or trigger invalid database queries.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in groups_controller.rb, the code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`. The finding claims these are 'unbounded and negative' which could cause issues. However, examining the code: 1) For limit, if a user passes a very large number, it would query many records, but this is a common pattern and the default is 50. 2) For offset, `.to_i` on nil returns 0, and negative offsets in SQL typically just return from the beginning. 3) The admin controller at line 35 does have `offset = Math.min(this.get('user_count'), Math.max(this.get('offset'), 0))` which bounds offset, but this is JavaScript client-side code. The Ruby controller doesn't validate these parameters. While unbounded limit could theoretically allow fetching all records (DoS concern) and negative offset could cause unexpected behavior, these are relatively minor issues. The finding overstates the severity - negative offset typically doesn't 'trigger invalid database queries' in most databases, it just behaves like 0 or returns empty results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2, confidence 100 — [group.js:23](/Users/dsifry/Developer/harnesseval/.cache/mrv_repos/9a4f0d24ab144b59/app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23) — After deleting the only member on the last page, the reload uses the stale pre-delete offset and leaves the UI on an empty out-of-range page.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when removeMember is called, it calls self.findMembers() after the deletion. The findMembers function calculates offset as Math.min(this.get('user_count'), Math.max(this.get('offset'), 0)). However, at the time findMembers is called after removal, the local user_count hasn't been updated yet - it still has the old value. The server will return the new total in result.meta.total, but the offset sent to the server is calculated using the stale user_count. If you're on the last page with 1 member and delete them, the offset would still be the old value (e.g., 50 if limit is 50 and there were 51 users), but now there are only 50 users. The server would return an empty result for that offset. This is a real edge case bug where deleting the last member on the last page could result in an empty/out-of-range page display.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3, confidence 75 — [admin/groups_controller.rb:65](/Users/dsifry/Developer/harnesseval/.cache/mrv_repos/9a4f0d24ab144b59/app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65) — Batch addition accepts an unbounded username list and performs a lookup plus association work inside the loop, producing N+1-style database traffic.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the add_members method in admin/groups_controller.rb lines 62-76, the code does iterate through usernames.split(',') and performs a User.find_by_username lookup for each username, then calls group.add(user). This is indeed an N+1 pattern where each username requires a separate database query. However, this is a valid finding - the code performs N database lookups (one per username) plus N association operations. While the group.save at the end is a single operation, the loop does create N+1-style database traffic for the user lookups. This is a real performance issue, though the severity depends on typical usage (how many users are typically added at once).
